public_rationale: The IEA's April 2025 illustration assigns 25 MW to a conventional data centre and 100 MW to a hyperscale data centre, giving a fourfold ratio [e1](https://build-up.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2025-04/PChtNmAZVk_11_04_2025_145800.pdf). IREN reports approximately 50 MW of capacity at Prince George as of December 31, 2025, with all mining hashrate capacity displaced to accommodate GPUs [e2](https://cdn.yahoofinance.com/prod/sec-filings/0001878848/000187884826000015/iren-20251231.htm). Neither provides a representative comparison of AI facilities with social-media or streaming facilities at August 25, 2026, so these examples do not settle the claimed 10-to-100-fold range [e1](https://build-up.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2025-04/PChtNmAZVk_11_04_2025_145800.pdf) [e2](https://cdn.yahoofinance.com/prod/sec-filings/0001878848/000187884826000015/iren-20251231.htm).
limitations: The IEA illustration compares conventional and hyperscale categories, without matching AI facilities to social-media or streaming facilities.
Prince George is one historical example without a matched comparator.
The packet lacks representative target-date data matching power definitions, building or campus boundaries, and operating or planned status.
Electrical capacity does not establish physical area, actual electricity consumption or energy per computation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers are 10 to 100 times larger and more power-intensive than those used for social media or streaming.

statement.excerpt: Data centers for AI are anywhere from 10 to 100 times larger and more power-intensive than those used for things like social media or streaming.

from_speaker: those used for things like social media or streaming
our_interpretation: The context measures size in megawatts, so the main comparison is facility electrical capacity. Physical floor area and energy per computation are not silently substituted.
The passage includes announced AI projects. Operating capacity and announced ultimate capacity must therefore be identified separately.
The ordinary reading is a general facility-level comparison, not a ratio constructed by selecting the largest AI campus and the smallest conventional building.

There is no common reporting quarter for these facilities. I use the inventory and capacity state immediately before publication on August 25, 2026; earlier snapshots provide context unless persistence is established.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable, sufficiently representative facility data show AI capacity generally within the asserted 10-to-100-fold range relative to social-media or streaming facilities, with consistent facility boundaries and project status.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable, sufficiently representative data show that the asserted range does not describe the two facility classes. Selected extremes or comparisons of campuses with individual buildings are insufficient.
